title: Computer Basics: CPU, Memory, Generations and Number Systems: Quiz

questions.question: Which part of the CPU directs the other components and decodes instructions but does no calculation itself?
questions.rationale: The Control Unit fetches, decodes and coordinates. The ALU performs arithmetic and logic, which is the usual swap.

questions.question: How many bits are there in 3 KB (using 1 KB = 1024 bytes)?
questions.rationale: 3 x 1024 = 3072 bytes and 3072 x 8 = 24,576 bits. 3072 is the byte count, the tempting wrong option.

questions.question: Which memory is volatile?
questions.rationale: RAM loses its content when power is off. ROM, disk and DVD keep data without power.

questions.question: Which of these is the FASTEST memory: Hard disk, RAM, Register, Cache?
questions.rationale: Registers sit inside the CPU and are the fastest, then cache, RAM and the hard disk.

Which of the following is NOT an input device?
questions.rationale: A plotter draws large diagrams, so it is an output device. The others feed data into the computer.

questions.question: Which technology marks the third generation of computers?
questions.rationale: Third generation (about 1964 to 1971) used ICs. Vacuum tubes were first, transistors second and microprocessors fourth.

questions.question: The hexadecimal number 2F is equal to which decimal number?
Which reader is used to process magnetic ink characters on bank cheques?
questions.rationale: MICR reads magnetic ink characters. OMR reads marked bubbles and OCR reads printed text.

questions.question: Which statement about translators is correct?
options: An interpreter converts the whole program at once
A compiler translates the whole program into machine code before running
A compiler works line by line
questions.rationale: A compiler translates the whole program; an interpreter goes line by line; an assembler converts assembly language.

questions.question: Add the binary numbers 1101 and 1011. The result is:
Which pair of generation and feature is correctly matched?
questions.rationale: The fourth generation is built on microprocessors (VLSI). Fifth generation is AI-oriented.

questions.question: Which memory type can be erased using ultraviolet light?
questions.rationale: EPROM is erased by UV light; EEPROM is erased electrically and PROM is programmable only once.
